messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I don’t know the will’s wording or whether the executor has started the process. I don’t have a price from A, and I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase. I don’t know what B needs or when. I want a fair share, but there’s no rush from my side. You can share that with them.

Thank you. I want to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but I haven’t settled on a price or timeline, and C’s agreement is needed. I’d be open to an independent valuation; how it’s paid for isn’t decided. I need to check whether we’d need a mortgage, and I haven’t read the will closely enough to say what it provides. Price and affordability matter most to me.

Thank you. Money toward starting a dance studio would help me most; sale proceeds seem the clearest route, though I don’t know what amount or timing is possible. I can’t give a firm deadline, and I’m not sure about A buying at a discount—I’d want the terms to be fair. I haven’t read the will, so I don’t know what it says. I’d like my sisters to understand that building the studio matters a great deal to me.

Mostly right. I’d clarify NCE 2: no discount or effect on anyone’s share has been agreed, and we don’t yet know what the will provides. I support an independent valuation; I don’t think you’re pushing that too hard.

That seems right to me. An independent valuation sounds sensible, and I agree we should first find out what the will says and who the executor is. A clear discount figure and a fallback for my studio money would help too.

That’s mostly right. I haven’t agreed to a discount, and I don’t know what our legal shares are, so don’t state the discount as money taken from them as a fact. An independent valuation seems sensible; I’m not agreeing to a price before we know what the will says.

I’d move Step 5 before Step 3: I should check financing and affordability before putting forward a price. I’d also make Step 6 conditional on the will, executor and legal process allowing it; an automatic sale date isn’t agreed.

I’d move Step 5 before Steps 3–4: I’d want to know A can finance the proposed price before C and I decide whether to accept it. And Step 4 should be subject to what the will and executor allow; I’m not sure we can assume our approval is legally required. I’d also want a firm fallback date, not “whenever A is ready.”

I can look for the will and ask Dad’s solicitor who the executor is. I’d change Step 4: my agreement is needed for me to accept a discount, but we shouldn’t assume that my or B’s yes/no alone decides what can legally happen before we know the will and our rights. And I wouldn’t set a fallback date yet; there’s no rush from me.
